# Choosing the project

The organization always comes from the credential. The project comes from
`project` when it is set, and from the credential otherwise: the owning user's
active project, or the project a service account is pinned to.

`project` takes a project id. Terraform resolves nothing at configuration time,
so a project name would be sent as it is and match no project.
`nemau project list` prints the ids. The value defaults to `NEMAU_PROJECT_ID`.

## Several projects with one credential

One credential can serve several projects. Declare one `alias` configuration
per project, differing only in `project`:

```terraform
provider "nemau" {
  alias   = "prod"
  project = var.prod_project_id
}

provider "nemau" {
  alias   = "staging"
  project = var.staging_project_id
}

resource "nemau_network" "prod" {
  provider = nemau.prod
  name     = "prod"
}

resource "nemau_network" "staging" {
  provider = nemau.staging
  name     = "staging"
}
```

The project is set per provider configuration. Resources have no `project`
argument, so a resource in another project needs its own `alias`.

A service account pinned to a project cannot use another one: the API answers
`403` and names the project it is attached to.

The [multi-project example](https://github.com/nemau-cloud/terraform-provider-nemau/tree/main/examples/multi-project)
declares a network and a subnet in two projects.
